newsitem.title: UK: WORLD BONDS-Wheezy yen dampens enthusiasm for JGBs.
newsitem.headline: WORLD BONDS-Wheezy yen dampens enthusiasm for JGBs.

text.p: International investor appetite for Japanese government bonds (JGBs) continues to be dulled by the weakness of the yen, analysts said on Friday.
But this has had a paradoxical effect on domestic investors who are reluctant to try overseas markets and risk currency losses, they said.

JGBs are likely to outperform against both U.S. and European bond markets after the Bank of Japan's quarterly report on Friday showed the economic recovery was weak to moderate, thus reducing the need for an immediate increase in interest rates.
"It is basically a Japanese liquidity story," said Kirit Shah, chief market strategist at Sanwa International in London.

"From an international perspective JGBs hold little intrinsic value unless you're a yen based player or unless you are expecting a significant correction in dollar/yen. But that won't happen in the near term and pressure on the yen will continue," he said.
At 1135 GMT, the yen was trading at 113.30 per dollar, but Shah said it would need to get past 110.00 to boost bond investor confidence.

"Being short of the yen is no longer a one-way bet," said Mark Capleton, international bond strategist at BZW in London. "Therefore Japanese investors are more reluctant to invest in foreign markets and accept the currency exposure."
He said profit taking on the yen had brought some money back into the domestic market, while overseas interest was mostly from Japanese institutions in external markets.
Analysts said JGBs had been boosted by the Bank of Japan's quarterly economic outlook which was bond friendly.

In it the Bank said the recovery of the Japanese economy was on the whole likely to be maintained in the coming months but would be restrained by pressure from various structural adjustments and from fiscal policies.
"One of the technical features (helping JGBs) is that the market has moved well away from seeing an interest rate increase at any time in the forseeable future," said Capleton.
He said from a domestic persepctive another feature had been the recent official buying of JGBs.
"A notable fund has been created to deal with the bad loans from some of the city banks. This has been parking money in JGBs which will ultimately be used to deal with bad debts," he said.

December JGB futures made a new all-time high on Friday, pushing up to 124.68 before easing to close at 124.49 in Tokyo. At 1052 GMT, LIFFE December JGB futures were testing that high and were trading at 124.66.
The 10-year benchmark JGB was yielding 2.620 percent, but Shah said further gains would be limited.
"JGBs will struggle to make new highs. We can go to 2.5 (percent) but there'll be selling pressures there," he said.
Capleton agreed. "The recent low was around two and a half on the 10-year yield. There may be some technical investors pushing to test that low but it's a pretty dangerous game."
However some analysts said JGBs still had scope to outperform.

"The rally has gone a long way but I don't see the market coming to any harm," said Mark Cliffe, chief economist at HSBC Markets in London. "The market is still fairly attractive and is farily well insulated from the problems we might see in other markets at the moment."

He said bond markets would be somewhat nervous of the U.S. over the next couple of weeks with important economic data releases and the U.S. presidential election, but this was unlikely to affect JGBs.
"The Japanese market seems to go on its own sweet way. There is no reason for a major selloff in the near term," he said.
